title: PROM ROYALTY
full_story:
Both Flora and North Clay High Schools held their proms on Saturday.

At the Flora Prom, Makenna Hackney the daughter of Joel and Sarah Hackney, was crowned Queen and Benny Allen the son of Ben Allen and Nicole Allen was crowned King.

The Flora High School Prom was held at the New Beginnings Church with the theme “Midnight on the River.”

The North Clay High School crowned Faith Jones the daughter of Julie Jones and Jonathan Jones as Queen, and Cody Zimdars the son of Randy and Shelly Zimdars, as King.  The theme at North Clay was “under the Sea.”

title: CLAY COUNTY MOBILE HOME TAXES
full_story:
The 2026 Mobile Home Privilege Tax Bills were mailed out last Monday.  The due date for mobile home taxes will be July 1st, but you can pay the taxes at any time.  After July 1st, you will be charged an additional $25.00 per month.

If you do not receive a mobile home Privilege tax bill, and you own a mobile home, please contact the Treasurer’s office immediately at 618-665-3727 or email [email protected].  That will give the office time to investigate the matter before it is at risk of becoming delinquent.

Clay County taxpayers can pay their mobile home taxes by mail by sending their check with the payment stub to the Clay County Treasurer PO Box 88 Louisville 62858.  Mailed payments must be postmarked on or before the due date to avoid penalty.  Mobile home privilege tax bills can be paid at the Treasurer’s office in the Clay County Courthouse, they accept cash, check, cashier’s check, or money orders.  Please bring your entire bill if you want it stamped to show proof of payment.  The Clay County Treasurer’s office hours are from 8 am to 4 pm and they are open during the noon hour.  Payment can be made by placing payment in the envelope depository at the north entrance of the Clay County Courthouse.  Please include payment stub.  Tax Bills can also be paid online by credit/debit card by going to govpaynow.com PLC number a00082.

title: CEO TRADE SHOW
full_story:
The Clay County CEO (Creating Entrepreneurial Opportunities) Class of 2026 will host its annual Trade Show on Wednesday night from 5:00 to 7:00 PM at the New Beginnings Church in Flora, where nine student entrepreneurs will showcase the individual businesses, they have developed throughout the school year.

The trade show represents the culmination of a year-long experience in which students learn the fundamentals of business by creating and operating their own ventures.  Community members are invited to attend, meet the students, and explore a wide variety of products and services created by local high school seniors.

Andrew Shelby, owner of HydroHoops, offers custom hydrodipped basketballs that feature unique, eye-catching designs, helping players easily identify their ball while expressing personal style.

Carder Walden created G2G (Glory to God), a Christian bracelet brand featuring high-quality woven bracelets with Bible verses printed on the inside, designed to inspire faith and spark meaningful conversations.

Chloe Whitmire, owner of Chloe’s Cleaning Co., provides residential and commercial cleaning services focused on reliability, attention to detail, and creating clean, welcoming environments.

Ella Cammon operates Essentials by Ella, a business that designs and sells organized, easy-to-use emergency car kits aimed at helping drivers feel safe and prepared for unexpected situations.

Halle Kitley brings creativity to the forefront with Patched Hat Bar, where customers can design their own custom trucker hats using a variety of patches and styles.

Haven Cash founded The Growing Point, a gardening brand offering curated boxes with seeds, guidance, and resources to help individuals and families learn and succeed in gardening.

Mason Byers, owner of Better Bites, produces protein balls and healthy snacks made with quality ingredients, offering a convenient and nutritious option for busy lifestyles.

Noah Hatcher created Fore You Golf, a custom golf accessory brand that allows golfers to personalize items such as balls, tees, markers, and towels.

Parker Helm launched LATHR, a men’s grooming brand specializing in high-quality scented soap bars designed to deliver premium fragrances and a refined grooming experience.

The Clay County CEO program emphasizes real-world learning by connecting students with local business leaders, providing mentorship opportunities, and allowing students to experience entrepreneurship firsthand.  The Trade Show serves as a final opportunity for students to present their work, engage with customers, and put their skills into action.

Community members are encouraged to attend and support these young entrepreneurs as they take an important step toward their futures in business and beyond.

title: WELDING COMPETITION
full_story:
Top high school welders put their skills to the test Thursday during the Sixth Annual Brandon Blackford Memorial Welding Competition hosted by the Olney Central College Welding Program.

The event featured 12 welders representing seven area high schools.  Winning first place, $500 and a welding hood was Finn Martin, of Mt. Carmel High School.  Second place, $400 and a welding hood was awarded to Trevin Hemrich, of Flora High School, and, third place, $300 and a welding hood went to Draven Taylor, of Flora High School.

Monetary awards were made possible by the Brandon Blackford Scholarship Fund, and Brandon’s family generously provided T-shirts for the event.

title: BLOOD DRIVE
full_story:
With a Blood Emergency in place throughout the Midwest, the American Red Cross is asking area blood donors to get out and give blood at their next earliest opportunity.

In response to the critical need for blood, the American Red Cross will have a blood drive tomorrow at the Flora High School from 8:30 am till 2 pm.  There are currently 8 Power Red Blood donation appointments available at this drive.  There are a number of Blood Drive appointments available and walk ins will be welcome.

Donors, especially those with type O blood and those giving platelets, can help bolster the blood supply now by making an appointment to give in the coming weeks.  Make an appointment to donate by downloading the free Red Cross Blood Donor App, visiting redcrossblood.org or calling 1-800-RED CROSS (1-800-733-2767).  A donor card, driver’s license, or two forms of ID are required at check-in.

Those who give blood or platelets at this drive will get a $15 e-gift card to the merchant of their choice.

After Tuesday’s drive the next Blood drive in our area will be on June 1st at Clay Electric COOP.

title: EASTERN ILLINOIS FOODBANK COMING
full_story:
The Eastern Illinois Foodbank will be in Clay County on Monday, May 11th to distribute food to area families facing food insecurity.  Those attending are asked to bring boxes or bags to transport their food in.

The Foodmobile will be at the Louisville Baseball Field where they will be distributing food from 9:30 until 10:30 am.

Those planning to attend should pre-register at www.EIFclient.com, although doing so does not guarantee a place in line.  There are some income guidelines.

The distribution is part of the Foodbank’s Foodmobile Program, a system of mobile food pantries designed to help bring nutritious food to rural or underserved areas.

The Clay County Ministerial Alliance food pantry is open every Monday from 9 to 11 am, at 1101 Austin Avenue in Flora.

title: 6K FOR WATER
full_story:
The 2026 6k for Water will be held on Saturday, May 16th for walkers and runners from all over Southern Illinois.  This is the 10th year for Flora’s 6k for Water where people come together to raise money for clean water.  703 million people worldwide lack access to clean water.

Flora’s 6k for Water partners with the Christian Humanitarian Organization, World Vision.  In the past 9 years, Flora has raised over $60,000 for efforts that dig wells, build rain catchments, teach hygiene and more through World Vision.

6 kilometers or 3.7 miles, is the average distance that women and children all over the world walk daily for water.  As a result, children do not get the chance to go to school, they have the fear of being kidnapped and being trafficked.  Clean water within a village equals freedom from those things.  Nearly 800 children die each day from water-related illnesses.  You can help bring clean water to these communities.  World Vision reaches a new person with clean water every 10 seconds.

Sign up for the 6k at https://global6k.worldvision.org/teams/Flora2026

The race begins at 9 AM at the Flora First Christian Church.  No need to attend FCC to join.  This is a community event.

Each registration equals clean water for 1 person for the rest of their life.

The Flora 6k for Water will be held on Saturday, May 16th, at 9 AM at the Flora First Christian Church.

title: ICASH RECORD
full_story:
Illinois Treasurer Michael Frerichs announced Thursday that he has returned over $2.5 billion in missing money on his watch, breaking all records in an I-Cash program that has been around since the 1960’s.

More than 2.5 million people, nonprofits, and businesses have been reunited with their missing money since Frerichs took office in 2015.  Frerichs modernized I-Cash, allowing people to file electronic claims, taking on powerful insurance companies to return money to beneficiaries, and cross-referencing state databases to return money without people even needing to file a claim.

A recent missing money return that helped eclipse the $2.5 billion mark was sending the $440,000 left by the late Joseph and Emilia Maldonado to St. Jude Children’s Research Hospital, a nonprofit that is seeking a cure for childhood cancer and other life-threatening diseases.

Joseph Maldonado was an engineer who came to the US from Argentina.  Emilia Maldonado worked in a factory after her family came to the US from Italy.  He passed in 2017 and she passed in 2022.  The couple thought highly of St. Jude, a top-rated national charitable organization.  Two years later, the couple’s bank turned the money over to the Illinois State Treasurer’s Office, as required by law, and the office worked to get the money to St. Jude.

Unclaimed property includes forgotten or overlooked bank accounts, uncashed rebate checks, unpaid life insurance claims, and the contents of abandoned safe deposit boxes.  When companies and banks cannot return these items to the rightful owners, by law, they are turned over to the Illinois State Treasurer’s Office.  The State Treasurer is legally required to return unclaimed property to its owners or their heirs, no matter how long it takes.

A key fight in Frerichs’ efforts to reform the unclaimed property program was taking on the insurance industry.  Previously, some life insurance companies did not pay death benefits when they knew, or should have known, a customer died.  State Treasurer’s audits found more than $550 million in death benefits that were not paid to grieving families in Illinois.  Treasurer Frerichs changed this unethical practice by working with state lawmakers to approve legislation that established the Unclaimed Life Insurance Benefits Act.

As a result of Treasurer Frerichs’ efforts, more than $500 million in unclaimed life insurance policies has been paid directly to beneficiaries.

Frerichs also worked with lawmakers to allow for claims to more easily be filed electronically and to create the Enhanced Money Match program, which takes the “claim” out of unclaimed property by automatically returning money after some information is electronically verified.  The effort has returned more than $130 million to more than 870,000 people since 2018.

Also added was a “share” button on the I-Cash website to allow people to alert family and friends when they see there is missing money waiting to be claimed, as well as a Spanish-language I-Cash website.
